```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| echo: false

library(tidyverse)
library(jsonlite)
library(plotly)

# Load scraped park dimensions dataset
parks <- fromJSON("data/park_dimensions_factors.json") |>
  as_tibble()

# 2026 season data for macro plot
parks_current <- parks |>
  filter(season == 2026, split == "All")

fit <- lm(index_hr ~ avg_fence_distance, data = parks_current)
r_val <- cor(parks_current$avg_fence_distance, parks_current$index_hr, use = "complete.obs")
r2_val <- summary(fit)$r.squared

# Load Statcast individual home runs dataset
hr_data <- fromJSON("data/statcast_homeruns.json") |>
  as_tibble()

max_dist <- max(hr_data$dist, na.rm = TRUE)
min_dist <- min(hr_data$dist, na.rm = TRUE)
max_ev <- max(hr_data$ev, na.rm = TRUE)
avg_ev <- round(mean(hr_data$ev, na.rm = TRUE), 1)
```

::: {.glass-card}
### Exit Velocity vs. Hit Distance

```{r}
#| label: plot-hr-scatter
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| echo: false

p_hr <- plot_ly(
  data = hr_data,
  x = ~ev,
  y = ~dist,
  color = ~stand,
  colors = c("L" = "#38bdf8", "R" = "#f472b6"),
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "markers",
  text = ~paste0(
    "<b>", player, "</b> (", stand, "HB)<br>",
    "Stadium: ", stadium, " (", team, ")<br>",
    "Date: ", date, "<br>",
    "Exit Velo: ", ev, " mph<br>",
    "Distance: ", dist, " ft<br>",
    "Launch Angle: ", la, "°<br>",
    "Pitch: ", pitch_speed, " mph<br>",
    "<i>", des, "</i>"
  ),
  hoverinfo = "text",
  marker = list(
    size = 6,
    opacity = 0.65
  )
) |>
  layout(
    title = list(
      text = "<b>Exit Velocity vs. Hit Distance (Color by Batter Hand)</b>",
      font = list(color = "#ffffff", size = 16)
    ),
    paper_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)",
    plot_bgcolor = "rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.6)",
    xaxis = list(
      title = "Exit Velocity (mph)",
      gridcolor = "rgba(51, 65, 85, 0.4)",
      color = "#94a3b8"
    ),
    yaxis = list(
      title = "Hit Distance (ft)",
      gridcolor = "rgba(51, 65, 85, 0.4)",
      color = "#94a3b8"
    ),
    legend = list(
      font = list(color = "#e2e8f0"),
      title = list(text = "<b>Batter Hand</b>")
    )
  )

p_hr
```
:::

## 🏟️ Ballpark Dimensions vs. HR Factor

Explore how outfield fence distance, wall height, and stadium altitude govern home run rates across Major League Baseball.

::: {.glass-card}
```{r}
#| label: plot-macro
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| echo: false

p_macro <- plot_ly(
  data = parks_current,
  x = ~avg_fence_distance,
  y = ~index_hr,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "markers",
  text = ~paste0(
    "<b>", venue_name, "</b> (", team, ")<br>",
    "City: ", city, "<br>",
    "HR Factor: ", index_hr, "<br>",
    "Avg Fence Dist: ", avg_fence_distance, " ft<br>",
    "Elevation: ", elevation, " ft"
  ),
  hoverinfo = "text",
  marker = list(
    size = 12,
    color = ~color,
    line = list(color = "#ffffff", width = 1.5),
    opacity = 0.9
  )
) |>
  add_lines(
    x = ~avg_fence_distance,
    y = fitted(fit),
    line = list(color = "#3b82f6", width = 2.5, dash = "dash"),
    name = "OLS Trendline",
    hoverinfo = "none"
  ) |>
  layout(
    title = list(
      text = "<b>Fence Distance vs. Home Run Park Factor (2026)</b>",
      font = list(color = "#ffffff", size = 16)
    ),
    paper_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)",
    plot_bgcolor = "rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.6)",
    xaxis = list(
      title = "Average Fence Distance (ft)",
      gridcolor = "rgba(51, 65, 85, 0.4)",
      color = "#94a3b8"
    ),
    yaxis = list(
      title = "Home Run Factor (100 = MLB Average)",
      gridcolor = "rgba(51, 65, 85, 0.4)",
      color = "#94a3b8"
    ),
    showlegend = FALSE
  )

p_macro
```
:::

::: {.glass-card}
### Statistical Regression Summary

- **Correlation Coefficient ($r$):** `r round(r_val, 3)` (moderate negative correlation)
- **Coefficient of Determination ($R^2$):** `r round(r2_val, 3)`
- **Regression Equation:** `r sprintf("HR Factor = %.2f * (Avg Fence Dist) + %.1f", coef(fit)[2], coef(fit)[1])`

> **Key takeaway:** Shorter outfield fences strongly facilitate home run production. Each 1-foot decrease in average fence distance correlates with an increase in home run factor.
:::
